photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Suriap, a named Ute chief, wearing fringed and embroidered shirt, sash, leggings, and moccasins — documentary photo of Ute dress.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of five Ute men in traditional dress (beaded chokers, dentalium ornaments, quillwork sash, peace medal) alongside three White officials/interpreters; documentary photo showing Ute dress and adornment fits the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: carte-de-visite
photo.title: carte-de-visite (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio carte-de-visite portrait of a Ute woman wearing hoop earrings, a multi-strand necklace and a striped garment, documenting traditional dress and adornment of the Ute people.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a Ute chief wearing a beaded choker and metal ear ornaments with a blanket over his knees, a documentary photo of dress consistent with the claimed people.

photo.name: carte-de-visite
photo.title: carte-de-visite (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio carte-de-visite of three Ute women wearing traditional skin dresses with fringes, ponchos, beaded belts, and moccasins, documenting traditional Ute dress. This is a documentary studio photograph of the people themselves, consistent with the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Documentary photograph of a Ute woman seated with a child in front of a brush-and-pole shelter (wickiup), with ceramic pots nearby — a traditional daily-life scene consistent with the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio portrait of two Plains men in decorated hide shirts, quillwork/beadwork, feather warbonnets, and leggings, consistent with Ute dress and documentary photo practice of the era.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: A documentary photo of a Ute girl in hide dress and fur robe holding a baby in a cradleboard, with drying meat/hide strips and a brush shelter behind her — consistent daily-life dress and material culture for the claimed people.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of two named Ute men (Wa-Rets and Shavano) in traditional dress with beaded chokers, fringed smocks, leggings, moccasins, and ornaments—documentary photo of Ute individuals in their own clothing/regalia.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a named Ute chief (Shavano) wearing a mix of Euro-American clothing with a fringed sash, beaded/bandolier bag, and decorated fringed rifle wrap — documentary photo of a Ute individual's dress and regalia, a valid subject even though taken in a Washington D.C. studio.

garment.name: moccasin; legging
garment.title: moccasin; legging
garment.reason: A pair of high hide leggings/moccasins with geometric beadwork (blue and white with hourglass motifs) and fringe, consistent with Ute woman's beaded legging-moccasins; museum credits Ute manufacture.

garment.name: hat
garment.title: hat
garment.reason: A twined rush basketry hat with a woven topknot, consistent with Ute/Great Basin conical basketry hats worn by women, made and used by the Ute.

garment.name: shirt
garment.title: shirt
garment.reason: Fringed hide shirt with beaded shoulder strips, dentalium/shell pendants, tin cones and deer-hoof tinklers is a classic Plains-style garment attributed by the museum to Ute makers; this matches known Ute hide clothing traditions.

household.name: basket; water-bottle
household.title: basket (?); water-bottle (?)
household.reason: A coiled, pitch-covered water-bottle basket with attached carrying handles — a classic Great Basin/Ute utilitarian water vessel form, consistent with Ute basketry traditions.

household.name: parfleche; quiver
household.title: parfleche; quiver
household.reason: This is a painted rawhide quiver with fringe, attributed by the museum to Ute makers — a plausible Plains/Plateau-style hide container made and used by the Ute. It is a container/utensil object, fitting household use broadly.
